name: tdd
description: 1. **STOP** — Understand the requirement. Write nothing yet. 2. **RED** — Write the smallest failing test that captures the requirement. Run it. Confirm it fails with the right error. 3. **GREEN** — Write the minimum production code to make the test pass. description: Use when CVE tickets land on the wrong team because a multi-app image confused the agent's service mapping. Covers building an image-to-service map from deployment manifests and forcing the agent to look up instead of guess. Not for scanner false positives.

name: the-agent-fixed-the-symptom-in-ci-conf-c0e55582234442d8
description: Fixes agents that patch CI config to make a test green in the pipeline while it still fails on developer machines. Use when CI is green, local runs are red, and the change touched only CI config. Reproduce locally, make the test hermetic so it passes anywhere, and validate config changes against a dev machine. Not for intentionally CI-only tests, and not for documented, accepted environment differences.

name: the-agent-grouped-cves-by-package-name-04fb39773fed8f0b
description: Use when CVE grouping by display name splits one library's findings across its old and new names. Covers PURL-based canonical identity, maintaining a rename-alias map, and fixing the remediation to cover both. Not for genuinely distinct libraries.

name: the-agent-hallucinated-blocklist-entri-26b02fac35c477c4
description: Stops an agent hallucinating blocklist entries that were never published, by requiring entries to cite a verified indicator source before sync. Use when downstream filters receive block entries with no corresponding approved indicator. Not for legitimate entries whose publication record is merely misfiled.

name: the-agent-hit-nvd-s-403-rate-limit-eve-40aa43f67fd7d566
description: Fixes NVD API 403 rate-limit errors by replacing per-CVE requests with batched, cached bulk pulls. Use when the agent makes one NVD request per CVE even with an API key, or when enrichment jobs die on 403s. Key trigger: request count scales with CVE count instead of staying flat.

name: the-agent-keeps-chasing-the-failing-te-94d464f01df16d58
description: An upstream-first debugging discipline for state leaks: when the failing test's logs show nothing wrong, the corruption came from an earlier passing test, and more log-reading on the victim is wasted effort. Use when repeated victim-focused investigation keeps coming up empty. Not for failures where the victim's own logs actually show the defect.

name: the-agent-kept-re-quarantining-the-sam-c24257470fcee441
description: Fixes an agent that keeps re-quarantining the same message after its release action fails, by checking action results and escalating instead of retrying blindly. Use when a release or quarantine action loops on one message across runs. Not for messages that genuinely need re-quarantining after re-delivery.

name: the-agent-keyed-tickets-on-cve-plus-im-f07b5ad810e44181
description: Fixes mass re-filing of findings when image tags get rebuilt by keying tickets on the immutable image digest instead of the mutable tag. Use when every finding re-files as new overnight after a tag rebuild. Key trigger: dedup keyed on CVE plus image tag, tag rebuilt, everything re-filed as new.

name: the-agent-leaked-its-nvd-api-key-into-aae7850fe7f03bb0
description: Recovers from an NVD API key leaked into agent logs via rotation, log redaction, and secret-store sourcing. Use when a key appears in log output, or when rotating a key breaks scheduled enrichment jobs that had it hardcoded. Key trigger: the same key value shows up in more than one place.

name: the-agent-marked-a-cve-fixed-but-the-r-1c2c86de3a1de720
description: Fixes a CVE that a rescan still flags after patching, because the patch bumped the package in the builder stage while the vulnerable copy ships in the final stage. Use it when the lockfile shows the fixed version but the scanner keeps reporting the CVE on the built image. Key trigger: the installed package version differs between build stages of a multi-stage Dockerfile.

name: the-agent-marked-a-cve-not-exploitable-b6dc7b2a1ce1d744
description: Rebuilds an auditable evidence trail behind 'not exploitable' verdicts: every such verdict must carry the call path or the proof of its absence, the code revision checked, and a VEX statement with justification. Use it when an auditor asks for the basis of a verdict and the ticket is empty. Key trigger: a 'not exploitable' verdict with no attached evidence.

name: the-agent-overwrote-trivyignore-with-i-dad7ae8bd8022a94
description: Use when a scan agent manages .trivyignore and the team's hand-curated suppressions disappeared. Covers restoring the curated file, switching the agent to append-only output, and locking the file against future overwrites. Not for trivy scan failures or for writing the initial ignore list.

name: the-agent-paged-on-call-for-a-cve-in-a-c0cf5a08716c66a1
description: Use when CVE alerts fire against workloads that are paused, draining, or being decommissioned. Covers feeding workload state into alert routing, suppressing pages for dead namespaces, and keeping a decommission list the agent reads. Not for active-workload CVE triage.

name: the-agent-parsed-red-hat-s-csaf-feed-b-53e3190dbed15c88
description: Replaces a hand-rolled Red Hat CSAF parser with spec-based parsing so moved fields stop breaking patch detection. Use when fixed versions look missing after a CSAF feed update, or when the agent parses CSAF JSON by field position. Key trigger: patch data vanished with no change in your code.

name: the-agent-posted-the-triage-summary-to-dedcaf9a45ab5909
description: Use when security alerts go to the wrong channel and the right team misses them. Covers config-driven channel routing, validating destinations at startup, and confirming delivery. Not for alert content or triage quality.

name: the-agent-processed-the-backlog-in-sev-0d0e440f720b5ec2
description: Use when a triage run re-processes items because live feed updates re-sorted the backlog mid-run. Covers snapshotting the work list at run start, deferring rescores to the next run, and resumable progress. Not for genuinely new CVEs arriving mid-run.

name: the-agent-quarantined-a-test-for-flake-b6df96f26047874b
description: Rescues a test that was quarantined as a flake when it was actually catching a real deploy config error. Use it when a skipped test turns out to be the only signal for a config or environment mistake in the release pipeline. Not for tests that genuinely flake on timing, and not for deploy failures with no test coverage at all.

name: the-agent-ran-trivy-with-severity-high-9feae3c6a956e22b
description: Use when a severity filter hid a KEV-listed CVE and the report claimed zero findings. Covers rescanning without the filter, making KEV membership override severity filters, and KEV-first triage. Not for tuning severity thresholds in general.

name: the-agent-re-triaged-the-same-backlog-14c5c712125bd0b4
description: Fixes a triage agent that re-processes its whole backlog repeatedly because the last-seen timestamp never reaches the database. Use it when every run treats all findings as new even though prior runs completed. Key trigger: the last-seen column in the database is null or frozen at an old date while runs keep succeeding.

name: the-agent-s-api-key-was-revoked-mid-ca-4d0284e95357756f
description: Handles an agent whose URL reputation API key was revoked mid-campaign, restoring access legitimately and degrading triage gracefully meanwhile. Use when reputation lookups suddenly fail with key errors during an active campaign. Not for keys that hit a usage quota, which recover with time or a plan change.

name: the-agent-s-ast-grep-rewrite-rule-kept-8894b45233bb1f00
description: Fixes an ast-grep rewrite rule that loops, appending the same import on every scan because the pattern matches its own insertion. Use when ast-grep update-all grows the file each run. Key trigger: the import count increases with every scan.

name: the-agent-s-bisection-found-no-culprit-1973b77286904a9e
description: Extends bisection past single-test removal when the order dependency needs three specific tests in sequence to trigger. Use it when the agent's bisect found nothing because removing any one test hides the failure. Not for single-polluter ordering bugs that bisect finds fine, and not for timing flakes unrelated to test order.

name: the-agent-s-browser-automation-failed-d4e4b85e6babdc03
description: Fixes an agent browser automation failing on a bank portal login when the MFA push never arrives: switch the step to a channel the portal supports unattended, add a human-approval checkpoint, or move to an API or file channel. Use when MFA blocks automation. Not for wrong usernames or passwords.

name: the-agent-s-campaign-report-exceeded-t-03bf7d538db3276f
description: Fixes a campaign report that exceeds the context limit so its IOC list never exports, by generating the IOC list with code and the narrative separately. Use when reporting fails at the export step on large campaigns. Not for small campaign reports that fit comfortably.

name: the-agent-s-codemod-added-the-same-esl-277b5b3166886266
description: Fixes a codemod that appends the same eslint-disable comment on every run. Use when files grow a new duplicate comment with each pass and re-linting never converges. Key trigger: N identical disable comments after N runs.

name: the-agent-s-codemod-converted-200-file-dedbf43017351526
description: Fixes resuming a codemod that crashed after converting 200 files, leaving the repo half on the old API. Use when tests fail both ways and the transform needs a safe resume point. Key trigger: git shows ~200 modified files and the rest still use the old API.

name: the-agent-s-credential-expired-mid-swe-9c006ea888818e3e
description: Restores a triage agent whose credential expired mid-sweep and broke mailbox access, by rotating to a longer-lived credential model and adding expiry monitoring. Use when mailbox access fails across a sweep with credential errors. Not for a single mailbox permission removal.

name: the-agent-s-csv-parser-broke-on-the-ba-ea94531fe60d4b10
description: Fixes an agent CSV parser breaking on a bank's semicolon-delimited file with quoted newlines: configure the parser for the real dialect, delimiter, quoting, and line endings, instead of assuming commas. Use when the file is valid but the parser reads it wrong. Not for files that are genuinely corrupt.

name: the-agent-s-cvss-recompute-disagreed-w-0ff8fa0fe6ffc928
description: Use when an agent recalculated a CVSS score, disagreed with NVD, and replaced the official score in the ticket. Covers restoring NVD as source of truth, storing the agent's score separately, and requiring human sign-off for overrides. Not for disputing a genuinely wrong NVD score.

name: the-agent-s-data-migration-copied-60-p-6f011f107147aeda
description: Fixes resuming a bulk data copy that died at 60 percent with no transaction and no watermark. Use when re-running the backfill would duplicate rows. Key trigger: the connection dropped mid-copy; batches weren't idempotent.

name: the-agent-s-debian-security-tracker-sc-ba1dad8ea8f3736b
description: Fixes Debian security tracker scrapers that broke when the tracker moved to a JSON format by switching from HTML scraping to the tracker's JSON data endpoint. Use when an agent's Debian tracker scrape returns empty or garbage after the format change. Key trigger: Debian security tracker scrape broke on the new JSON format.

name: the-agent-s-dedup-keyed-on-image-diges-bbc68c224540e809
description: Use when a registry retag makes one digest look like two images and the report contradicts itself. Covers tracking tag-to-digest history, fixing the dedup key, and reconciling the report. Not for genuinely distinct images sharing layers.

name: the-agent-s-defender-api-session-broke-6f5a282588a0736e
description: Restores a triage agent Defender API session broken by a password or credential rotation it did not know about, by moving the agent to rotation-proof credentials. Use when API access breaks immediately after an account credential change. Not for rotations the agent was notified of and updated for.

name: the-agent-s-diff-flagged-every-defined-265a4cf32dc3d0d9
description: Fixes diffs that flag every defined term as changed when the counterparty just capitalized them all: casing treated as substantive. It shows how to compare defined terms case-insensitively and keep casing as display-only. Use it when a capitalization pass floods your redline with term changes that mean nothing.

name: the-agent-s-diff-flagged-the-entire-si-27f90f6c252f9a5f
description: Fixes diffs that flag the whole signature block as deleted when the counterparty switches page size, like Letter to A4, shifting every page break. It shows how to diff at the paragraph level ignoring pagination, and how to treat signature blocks as structured content. Use it when a page-size or margin change makes your redline agent report deletions that are really just repagination.

name: the-agent-s-diff-treated-a-reordered-e-21cf4258b9128baa
description: Fixes exhibit-list diffs that report a reorder as 12 deletions plus 12 additions: the agent never realigned the list items. It shows how to match list items by content across versions, detect moves, and compare lists independent of order. Use it when reordered exhibits, schedules, or numbered lists produce deletion-heavy diffs that scare reviewers.

name: the-agent-s-exploitability-assessment-214b8933cbd14a91
description: Fixes an LLM triage agent that contradicts itself on whether a vulnerable function is reachable by making every verdict evidence-bound: no call path, no 'not reachable.' Use it when two runs of the same agent disagree on exploitability for identical code. Key trigger: contradictory reachability verdicts across runs with no code change.

name: the-agent-s-exploitability-verdict-rel-1f75d8cb6557acec
description: Use when exploitability verdicts change because advisory prose was reworded, not because facts changed. Covers evidence-backed verdicts, ignoring prose-only diffs, and versioning verdicts with evidence hashes. Not for new technical information in an advisory update.

name: the-agent-s-extraction-returned-comple-c2e66af36c3943f3
description: Fixes false 'complete' reports in contract extraction: the agent said extraction was complete while the last 30 pages of schedules never entered context. It shows how to gate the complete flag on an independent page count, verify pages-in equals pages-processed, and make incompleteness impossible to misreport. Use it when extraction reports success but you suspect trailing pages were never read.

name: the-agent-s-flyway-run-lost-its-connec-8eb613a6a073e291
description: Fixes a Flyway run where the schema history row committed but the data copy did not finish after a connection loss. It shows how to verify what data actually landed, remove the misleading history row, and re-run safely, plus how to split schema and data migrations so it cannot recur. Use when flyway_schema_history disagrees with the real table contents.

name: the-agent-s-ignore-rule-expired-silent-21099674b982de5c
description: Use when expired suppressions return as a flood of new findings with no warning. Covers re-applying after review, expiry notifications, and treating mass reappearance as an incident. Not for first-time triage of genuinely new CVEs.

name: the-agent-s-ioc-extractor-failed-on-ba-46a8562134d56872
description: Fixes an agent IOC extractor failing on base64-encoded message bodies, by decoding MIME parts before extraction. Use when indicators are missed because the body or attachment content arrives base64 encoded. Not for messages where indicators are absent for other reasons.

name: the-agent-s-jscodeshift-transform-doub-8ea4298c1f7b66e9
description: Fixes a jscodeshift transform that isn't idempotent and double-wraps components in React.memo on re-run. Use when a codemod changes its own output so running it twice produces different results. Key trigger: components wrapped in memo(memo(...)) after a second pass.

name: the-agent-s-kev-due-date-math-was-off-889d7c79fa012a02
description: Fixes KEV due-date math that flags CVEs as overdue a week early because of a timezone mix-up. Use it when a triage agent marks CISA KEV entries overdue that are not actually due yet. Key trigger: the overdue list shifts by exactly the UTC offset of the agent's timezone.

name: the-agent-s-kev-watch-checked-the-cata-ccf15dd2a26cafa5
description: Use when KEV due dates are computed from the wrong start date or the catalog is polled too slowly. Covers using CISA's dateAdded, polling daily, and recomputing open KEV tickets. Not for non-KEV CVE prioritization.

name: the-agent-s-kubectl-is-1-29-but-the-cl-866e677584e3a5f0
description: Fixes manifests rejected by the API server when the agent's kubectl is too new for the cluster. It shows how to confirm the version skew, install a matching kubectl, and validate server-side before applying. Use when kubectl applies fail against an older cluster.

name: the-agent-s-last-scan-watermark-advanc-190c52a002ce0dc8
description: Use when a scan watermark or checkpoint moved forward despite a failed scan, causing the next run to skip unscanned assets. Covers success-only watermark writes, resetting the watermark, and backfilling missed scans. Not for slow or partial scans that genuinely completed.

name: the-agent-s-nightly-fleet-scan-only-fi-52ec92c9e6f40fdb
description: Fixes nightly fleet scans that never finish in the maintenance window by parallelizing workers, caching the vulnerability DB once per host, and skipping unchanged image digests. Use when an agent scans a container fleet sequentially and only a fraction completes before the window closes. Key trigger: nightly scan finishes only 60 of 200 images.

name: the-agent-s-nvd-cve-feed-parser-broke-80f988cb47f12703
description: Fixes NVD feed parsers that silently match zero CVEs after the NVD 2.0 schema change by updating the configurations node path and adding a zero-match canary alert. Use when a CVE matcher returns no results overnight with no error after an NVD schema update. Key trigger: NVD parser broke and the matcher silently returned zero CVEs.

name: the-agent-s-one-click-unsubscribe-link-62f3c2ee4d19e0d9
description: Fixes a broken one-click unsubscribe link (404 or error page) that turns routine opt-outs into spam complaints and damages the sending domain's reputation. Use when unsubscribe links fail, return errors, or were never end-to-end tested. Not for deliverability issues with working links, or for consent and list-quality problems.

name: the-agent-s-one-pr-per-cve-policy-crea-23098480ec6fcdd8
description: Replaces a one-PR-per-CVE policy with root-cause grouping: when many CVEs trace to one shared transitive dependency, a single bump PR closes them all. Use it when the backlog is full of duplicate fix PRs for the same underlying package. Key trigger: many CVE tickets converging on one shared dependency.

name: the-agent-s-osv-aliases-parser-broke-w-7afefaea30f5ccab
description: Fixes an OSV aliases parser to read both the active and withdrawn alias arrays after the schema change. Use when alias lookups suddenly return nothing, or when dedup starts missing matches that used to resolve. Key trigger: OSV responses now carry a separate withdrawn aliases array your parser ignores.

name: the-agent-s-patch-validation-only-re-r-e9f84297b008d163
description: Use when patch validation checks the lockfile but the deployed artifact still carries the vulnerable layer. Covers validating the deployed image digest, wiring validation to post-deploy scans, and closing only on artifact evidence. Not for lockfile-only projects with no deployed image.

name: the-agent-s-pdf-parser-broke-on-a-smug-f28e89ffea045385
description: Fixes an agent PDF parser that breaks on an HTML smuggling sample carried in or beside a PDF, by separating document parsing from HTML analysis. Use when PDF parsing crashes or returns garbage on a smuggled or hybrid attachment. Not for scanned-image PDFs that need OCR.

name: the-agent-s-per-cve-nvd-lookups-took-6-61015edee0146438
description: Replaces per-CVE NVD API lookups with a locally synced bulk mirror for fast enrichment. Use when per-CVE lookups take hours, or when the enrichment pipeline's runtime is dominated by NVD round trips. Key trigger: enrichment time grows linearly with backlog size.

name: the-agent-s-prisma-migrate-diff-said-t-3125924a0fc17fb0
description: Fixes the confusion when prisma migrate diff says no-op but migrate deploy still has work to do. It explains that the two commands answer different questions - diff compares schema to database, deploy compares migration files to history - and shows the status-first workflow that removes the surprise. Use when Prisma's dry-run and deploy seem to disagree.

name: the-agent-s-prisma-migrate-lost-its-da-7e0465299c50b70b
description: Fixes a Prisma migration blocked by a failed row in _prisma_migrations after a lost database connection. Use when migrate deploy refuses to run until the failed migration is resolved. Key trigger: a row with finished_at null in _prisma_migrations; choose migrate resolve --applied vs --rolled-back.

name: the-agent-s-python-libcst-codemod-dupl-acf63b11417a5706
description: Fixes a Python libcst codemod that duplicates decorators on every run. Use when re-running a decorator-adding transform mid-migration isn't safe. Key trigger: the same decorator stacked N times after N runs.

name: the-agent-s-quarantine-list-silently-g-ac1349b0fc0aaefe
description: Shows how to force an agent to re-verify tests before quarantining when its quarantine list has silently grown to a large share of the suite. Use it when quarantine keeps growing without review and coverage is quietly shrinking. Not for one-off legitimate quarantines, and not for suites that have no quarantine mechanism at all.

name: the-agent-s-rag-chunking-cut-a-sentenc-13742357cee151f6
description: Fixes RAG chunking that splits legal sentences mid-clause and returns fragments that flip the meaning of contract language. Use when retrieved chunks end or start mid-sentence, or the agent answers from a clause fragment like "shall" that lost its "not". Key trigger: a retrieved chunk boundary falls inside a sentence containing a negation or a numeric limit.

name: the-agent-s-reachability-evidence-cite-a648796b289e69b2
description: Use when reachability verdicts cite files or SBOMs from a different build than the deployed image. Covers pinning evidence to the image digest, verifying file existence, and invalidating bad verdicts. Not for genuinely reachable vulnerable code.

name: the-agent-s-redline-tool-compared-the-a2a164e5f32a767f
description: Fixes a redline tool that compared the wrong file pair because a near-duplicate filename won the file lookup. Use when a diff reports phantom changes that do not exist between the versions you meant to compare, or the tool picks files by fuzzy name match. Key trigger: the compared filenames differ by a suffix like _CLEAN that the lookup ignored.

name: the-agent-s-remediation-pr-bumped-the-14a473af3d1b81e8
description: Use when a fix PR touched the wrong dependency scope and the finding survives. Covers mapping findings to the exact manifest path, reverting the wrong bump, and gating security PRs on rescan clearance. Not for version-resolution failures.

name: the-agent-s-send-tuesday-9am-rule-used-e31d21d7c32e89cc
description: Fixes an SDR agent whose 'send Tuesday 9am' rule runs on the server clock instead of the lead's timezone: replace server-local scheduling with per-lead timezone conversion and validate rendered local times before sending. Use when a weekday-morning rule lands at odd hours for distant leads. Not for UTC conversion bugs, DST shifts, or rep-vs-lead zone mixups.

name: the-agent-s-severity-override-was-lost-0dd5c56bc98e11b3
description: Use when analyst severity overrides vanish on scanner re-import and tickets snap back to the scanner's severity. Covers storing overrides outside the import, merge-not-overwrite imports, and round-trip testing. Not for first-time triage of new findings.

name: the-agent-s-shift-handoff-notes-refere-3278d37906f5d619
description: Fixes shift-handoff notes referencing the wrong campaign after a context overflow, by keying all handoff state to explicit campaign identifiers. Use when handoff summaries mix details between campaigns after long or overflowing runs. Not for handoff errors caused by a human editing the notes.

name: the-agent-s-slack-alert-loop-fired-400-9b658e76f73fe893
description: Use when an alert loop spams a channel with one message per finding until rate limits stop it. Covers stopping the loop, switching to digest alerts, and per-run message caps. Not for a single misrouted alert.

name: the-agent-s-stop-on-reply-check-ran-on-dc7db0a5becd6049
description: Fixes follow-ups going out after a lead already replied because the agent's stop-on-reply check only runs once a day. Use when replies and scheduled sends race each other and leads get follow-ups they already answered. Not for out-of-office auto-replies (those need classification, not stopping) or sequences meant to continue after a reply.

name: the-agent-s-suppression-file-wasn-t-ho-46b19641e7124859
description: Restores trivy suppression handling after a version upgrade by verifying which ignore file the new version reads, where it looks for it, and whether entries still match. Use it when previously suppressed CVEs return as fresh findings right after a trivy upgrade. Key trigger: ignore file unchanged, trivy version changed, suppressed CVEs back in the report.

name: the-agent-s-ticket-titles-used-the-sca-2b3ff7909fed42fa
description: Use when tickets are titled with scanner-internal IDs so nobody can find them by CVE. Covers renaming to CVE-first titles, storing internal IDs as metadata, and adding search aliases. Not for ticket content or triage quality.

name: the-agent-s-triage-loop-re-scanned-the-7d861f6d055e06e7
description: Use when a vuln-triage agent keeps re-scanning images it already scanned because its completion marker is unreachable. Covers fixing the marker path, writing markers only on success, and adding rescan-count alerts. Not for scanner timeouts or slow scans.

name: the-agent-s-triage-run-failed-after-th-271d60515fe9925b
description: Handles a triage run failing when the mailbox search API returns empty results mid-campaign, by distinguishing a true empty result from a failed or malformed query. Use when search-based sweeps intermittently return zero results for mail known to exist. Not for mailboxes that genuinely contain no matching mail.

name: the-agent-s-triage-state-didn-t-persis-4f31341ee601e50a
description: Fixes a CVE triage agent that loses its triage state between runs and re-scores the same 300-CVE backlog every night. Use it when every run starts from an empty or stale state even though the previous run completed. Key trigger: triage results exist in logs but never appear in the database or state store on the next run.

name: the-agent-s-trivy-server-mode-scan-hun-99367ffc4e024923
description: Diagnoses a hung trivy server-mode scan stuck on layer analysis, distinguishing a stalled download, an oversized layer, and a dead server from a scan that is merely slow. Use when a scan stalls with no progress output for tens of minutes on an "analyzing layer" line. Not for trivy client-mode errors, vulnerability DB download failures, or scans that finish but report no vulnerabilities.

name: the-agent-s-vex-statement-said-not-aff-6408c94fedce7efe
description: Use when a VEX not_affected claim is wrong because the component was vendored or renamed. Covers withdrawing the statement, proving absence properly, and requiring evidence on every not_affected. Not for genuinely absent components.

name: the-agent-s-weekly-vuln-report-double-e66c902b11ab06ec
description: Use when two scanners feed one dashboard and the numbers are inflated by duplicates. Covers canonical finding keys, ingest-time dedup, and recomputing the report. Not for a single scanner's accuracy problems.

name: the-agent-s-word-diff-ignored-a-delete-4a280d805f9b44c0
description: Fixes word-diffs that silently drop negations: punctuation normalization skipped a deleted 'not', so 'shall not disclose' became 'shall disclose' with no flag. It shows how to normalize punctuation without dropping word tokens, and how to report token deletions explicitly. Use it when a diff's normalization step can erase meaning-carrying words and your redline must never miss a negation change.

name: the-agent-said-flake-because-the-error-00262bc5f55b938e
description: Fixes test-healing agents that label a changing-error failure a flake when the real cause is an uninitialized random seed. Use when a test fails with a different error message on every run, especially under pytest-randomly or hypothesis, and reruns keep producing new failure modes. Pin the seed to reproduce the stable failure, then fix the real ordering or randomness bug underneath. Not for infrastructure flakes that fail with the same error, and not for tests with no randomness involved.

name: the-agent-said-not-reachable-but-the-v-e1c96da8b1a1b293
description: Closes the feature-flag blind spot in reachability analysis: enumerate build tags and runtime flags, check their production values, and treat flag-gated code as reachable unless the flag is provably off. Use it when a 'not reachable' verdict ignored configuration-gated code paths. Key trigger: the vulnerable function sits behind a flag the check never evaluated.

name: the-agent-said-snapshot-drift-but-the-4e27c920fb7e7956
description: Corrects the misdiagnosis where an agent labels a snapshot mismatch as drift when the component actually regressed. Use when a snapshot failure's stored value still matches the design spec, or when the agent wants to update a snapshot you suspect is correct. Not for snapshots that are genuinely outdated after an intentional redesign.

name: the-agent-scanned-the-staging-registry-12bd1707caea3450

Par exemple : « je veux créer une application », « je veux ajouter une fonctionnalité », « j'aimerais mettre en place » ou des questions comme : « que penses-tu ... ? », « comment je pourrais ... ? », « est-ce possible de ... ? »

name: think-argument-mapping
description: Produces an argument map by laying out a claim's supporting reasons, the co-premises each silently depends on, and the objections against it as an explicit structure, then flags the weakest links and unsupported premises. Use when an argument or recommendation must be evaluated for soundness, or when a fluent case may be hiding a broken inference.

name: think-around-problem
description: Always-on anti-satisficing — question everything (the human, docs, comments, research), explore alternatives in proportion to the stakes, never take the first workable answer.

name: think-assumption-reversal
description: Generates non-obvious ideas by surfacing the foundational assumptions a problem or solution rests on, negating each, and reframing from the reversed assumptions, then shortlisting, producing an assumptions-and-reversals sheet. Use when an option space feels stuck inside default constraints, or when you need to expose premises that are taken for granted.

name: think-at-hard-selective-refinement
description: Reduce reasoning model inference cost by selectively applying latent iterations—use a lightweight neural decider to identify hard tokens and refine only those with focused LoRA modules, achieving 94% token exemption with 8-11% accuracy gain.

name: think-augmented-function-calling-improving
description: Improve LLM function/tool calling accuracy by injecting explicit "think" reasoning parameters into function schemas before the model generates arguments. Based on the TAFC framework (arXiv:2601.18282). Use this skill when: - "Add reasoning to my tool definitions" - "My agent is passing wrong parameters to functions" - "Improve function calling accuracy for complex APIs" - "Debug why my LLM agent picks incorrect argument values" - "Make my tool calls more reliable with chain-of-thought" - "Augment my OpenAI function schemas with reasoning"

name: think-authentic-dissent
description: Checks whether a decision has genuine minority dissent or only smooth surface consensus, identifies who actually holds a contrary view, and plans how to elicit and protect real dissent, flagging clearly where a view is constructed rather than authentically held. Use when consensus feels too easy, or to set up genuine challenge before a high-stakes call.

name: think-backcasting
description: Produces a backcast path by fixing a vivid desired future state and reasoning backward through the milestones and preconditions required to reach it, ending at the next concrete step available now. Use when planning toward a transformative or long-horizon goal that forward planning anchors too low, when a chosen future needs a route mapped back to today, or when milestones and dependencies between now and the goal must be made explicit.

name: think-before-act
description: 元约束：先查再动手，列方案让用户审批，不蛮干。Use BEFORE any non-trivial action (debug/test/implement/refactor/fix/config/upgrade). Especially when facing silent failures, runtime errors not caught by compiler, or behavior that contradicts documentation.

name: think-before-code
description: Enforce a learning-focused, specification-first workflow for substantial software builds. Use when a learner or vibe coder must personally define users, behavior, scope, modules, material technologies, order, tests, and completion evidence before coding, without agent-supplied choices. Keep all user-facing replies in simple, controlled language. Do not use for conceptual questions, reviews, incident containment, or tiny fully specified edits unless explicitly invoked.

name: think-before-coding
description: Forces explicit reasoning before writing any code. Surfaces assumptions, manages confusion, and prevents hallucination by demanding clarity upfront.

name: think-before-coding
description: Use before writing or changing code on any non-trivial task, to surface hidden assumptions, keep the change minimal and surgical, and define how you will verify success. The discipline that stops over-engineering and wasted tokens before they happen.

name: think-before-coding
description: Guardrails for writing, modifying, reviewing, or refactoring code. Use whenever a task involves code to clarify ambiguous requirements before implementation, avoid over-engineering and speculative abstractions, and keep changes minimal and scoped.

name: think-before-coding
description: Use BEFORE writing any backend code (endpoint, worker, CLI, script, consumer, cron, pipeline, daemon, webhook handler, integration). Forces the 6-step senior workflow so the design is sound before the first line ships. If you are about to write a server-side component of any kind, you MUST invoke this first.

name: think-before-coding
description: Use before writing or changing any non-trivial code. Forces evaluation of at least three distinct solution approaches with brief trade-offs before implementing, so the chosen design fits the existing codebase instead of being the first idea that came to mind.

name: think-before-coding
description: Apply think before coding when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code.

name: think-before-coding
description: Surface assumptions and ambiguity before writing code. Use when a request has multiple valid interpretations, requires non-obvious assumptions, or when proceeding on a guess would cost more to undo than to clarify upfront.

name: think-before-coding
description: Use BEFORE writing any Spring Boot backend code (REST controller, @KafkaListener/@RabbitListener consumer, @Scheduled job, Spring Batch job, CommandLineRunner/admin task, outbound client, webhook receiver, JPA repository/service). Forces the 6-step senior workflow so the design is sound before the first line ships. If you are about to write a server-side component of any kind, you MUST invoke this first. Triggers also on "сделай эндпоинт", "напиши сервис", "добавь консьюмер", "новая джоба", "спроектируй", "реализуй фичу".

name: think-before-coding-surface-assumptions
description: Before implementing, surface assumptions, present multiple interpretations, and stop to ask when something is unclear. Use whenever a user request has ambiguous scope, fields, format, or behavior.

name: think-before-refusal
description: Prevents false-positive refusals and overly conservative censorship by applying a Think-Before-Refusal (TBR) intent analysis workflow and verifying copyright or licensing status on the web before declining a request. Use whenever a user prompt touches complex technical, security, medical, legal, creative, or deep-work topics that might trigger surface-level keyword sensitivity, or involves quoting, adapting, or processing works where copyright, public domain, Creative Commons, or open-source licensing applies.

name: think-before-ship
description: When designing, architecting, or building anything consequential (feature, module, cross-system change, strategy-shaped doc) before committing to a shape. Sizes the ask, writes a design note with real alternatives including a bold one, adversarial pass on large work, premise check, statechart for flows. Skips typos and one-line edits. Use in Cursor Plan mode, local chat, or before coding in a cloud agent run.

name: think-before-slides
description: 想清楚再做 PPT（汇报逻辑与逐页大纲助手）。慢想快做——在动手画幻灯片前，帮你把模糊想法和零散材料磨成有依据的 Markdown 逐页大纲、评审意见与讲稿。支持准备、素材、叙事、写作、评审、改稿反复调用，只出思路与逐页大纲，不负责最终 PPT 排版渲染。

name: think-belief-update-routine
description: Produces a belief-update ledger that re-scores a standing inventory of open beliefs against newly arrived evidence on a cadence - each belief carrying a prior confidence, the evidence accrued since the last review, a revised confidence with an explicit delta and direction, a reason for the size of the move (a guard against under-updating), and a next-review trigger. Use when you hold consequential open beliefs, forecasts, or standing assumptions that should track new evidence over time and you want a disciplined, recurring re-score - not a one-time decision record, a finished-event retro, or…

name: think-better
description: A reasoning routine for problems where a fast first answer is likely to be wrong. It covers framing the real question, separating facts from assumptions, weighing more than one candidate, not inventing numbers, stress-testing recommendations, and stating how confident you are. Use it for multi-step reasoning, math and estimation, logic puzzles (especially ones that look like a famous puzzle), debugging with an unclear cause, design or tradeoff decisions, ambiguous requests, and claims that need verifying. It includes an error-correcting pass, in which an independent critic subagent reviews th…

name: think-better
description: Structured opener for non-trivial tasks. Forces goal + decision criterion (and whether the work is finite or evergreen), an INTERVIEW decision (ask the principal the few things only they know before setting a direction, or name why not), approach in 2-3 bullets, one-line premortem, named verifier, and a routing decision (which branch / worktree the work lands on) before any tool calls. Evidence-aligned (Plan-and-Solve, Klein premortem, Anthropic evals-first); explicitly NOT a manufacturing-framework cargo cult. AUTO-TRIGGER on any of the following — do not wait for the user to invoke: a task…

name: think-big
description: Strategic thinking framework — analyze whether something is worth doing, what the risks are, and what the long-term impact will be. Use when user says 「战略思考」「战略分析」「从战略角度看」「战略视角」「帮我想清楚这件事」「这件事值不值得做」「从更高视角分析」 / think-big, strategic thinking, strategy. Not for execution-level planning (that's tactical).

name: think-big
description: Use this skill when the user asks to "think-big", think big, explore possible futures, map strategic possibilities, synthesize signals, generate scenarios, find second-order effects, identify opportunities, or challenge consensus around a broad theme in markets, products, technology, society, careers, companies, design, behavior, culture, or life. This skill is for disciplined strategic imagination: broad possibility exploration grounded in context, evidence, mechanisms, uncertainty, and useful provocations. Do not use it for generic brainstorming, generic research reports, automatic startup…

name: think-big
description: Explores a vast idea before /omni:brainstorm with a studio of agents that talk to each other — judges its scale and kind (a tweak gets the /omni:visual-fix line, a feature is offered /omni:brainstorm or a lite run), fuels the studio with today's product and world-class references, then runs rounds of rendered concepts, six to eight storyboard cards then clickable prototypes, that a panel of a Visionary, a Craft critic, a Skeptic, a Value critic and real users debates by name while the person reacts at every round and crowns one. Records the crowned concept, its vision tour, every board, the d…

name: think-big
description: Zoom out from building/executing mode and think big about how something you have already built (or are deep in) could grow and become profitable — an exit, a product, a partnership. Triggers on "think big about X", "how could this become profitable", "work backwards from the goal", "envision/manifest", or "could we sell/pitch this to <company>". Delivers grounded market comps and an honest current-stage number, then a concrete staged roadmap back to today — not just a vision statement.

name: think-big
description: Use this skill when the user says give me the 10x version of this plan, help me think bigger, pressure-test whether this goal is ambitious enough, challenge the constraints in this plan, reimagine this approach, run a door-type analysis, audit whether this plan is bold enough, or make this goal sound ambitious by multiplying every target by ten. It produces a 10x Plan with Door-Type Analysis or a Think Big Audit. It changes mechanisms and end states, tests assumptions, distinguishes reversible and hard-to-reverse choices, and pairs bold outcomes with evidence gates and a practical path. Even…

name: think-big-search-small-where-capacity-matters-in-hierarchical-search-agents
description: Large language model based search agents increasingly adopt multi-agent architectures in which a main agent decomposes a complex question into sub-queries and dispatches them to parallel sub-agents. H. Based on arXiv:2607.07548.

name: think-boundary-critique
description: Audits the boundary judgments that silently define a problem frame. For each of four sources, who benefits, who decides, whose knowledge counts, who has standing, it contrasts the descriptive is boundary against the normative ought boundary, names the gaps, and lists the affected-but-excluded parties who have no voice in the frame, producing a boundary-judgment audit rather than a stakeholder round-up. Use when a plan, metric, or proposal already encodes who matters and who does not and the risk is solving a tidy problem for the people inside the line while pushing harm onto people outside it…

description: Good-faith divergent brainstorming toward a goal. Validates assumptions and reframes the problem when its framing is in doubt, runs brainstormers using different techniques in isolation, and synthesizes standouts and hybrids. Produces feedback only.

description: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.

name: think-brainstorm
description: Good-faith divergent brainstorming for achieving a goal. Validates assumptions, then spawns brainstormers running different techniques (first-principles, working-backwards, lateral, analogical, constraints-shift, etc.) in isolation, and synthesizes the pool into a report of standouts, reasonable ideas, and hybrid combinations. Produces feedback only — no code, no tickets, no artifacts.

name: think-brainwriting
description: Generates ideas the way silent parallel brainwriting does, producing several independent idea streams that build on each other without anchoring on the first voice, then consolidates them into a shortlisted idea pool. Use when you need breadth of options and want to avoid the anchoring and conformity that make ordinary brainstorming underperform.

name: think-canvas
description: Work on a think canvas (the brainstorming app's boards) — start one, add or rearrange blocks, frames and links, answer comments, report back in its chat — with the `think` command. Use when asked to put something on a think canvas, start a board, map something out on a board, or read what was discussed there.

name: think-causal
description: Causal reasoning methods — Causal analysis (cause-effect mechanisms, causal graphs, confounders) and Counterfactual reasoning (what-if scenarios, alternative histories, intervention analysis). Use when the user invokes `/think causal` or `/think counterfactual`, or asks about cause-and-effect relationships, confounders, or "what would have happened if..." questions.

name: think-causal-layered-analysis
description: Produces a four-layer matrix (litany, system, worldview, myth) of the current 'used future' beside a reconstructed preferred future per layer, anchored by a deliberately changed deep metaphor. Use when an issue is stuck because the framing is stuck, the official account and the system explanation have been argued to exhaustion, and the real disagreement is about clashing worldviews and the unexamined story underneath. Not a single-cause diagnosis (that is think-iceberg-model) and not a forecast.

name: think-causal-loop-diagrams
description: Builds a signed causal loop diagram by closing the feedback loops in a situation, labeling each loop reinforcing (R) or balancing (B) with its link polarities, and reading likely dynamics (spiral, goal-seeking, or oscillation) off which loop dominates. Use when a situation feeds back on itself - growth that funds more growth, a fix that recreates its own problem, capacity that relieves then re-attracts demand - and you need to see why it keeps accelerating, stalling, or overshooting. Not for a single accumulation, a one-directional consequence tree, or a genuinely linear chain.

name: think-cell-charts
description: Build evidence-backed management PowerPoint slides from Excel/CSV or other structured business data using an enforced analysis → storyline → presentation-template → official think-cell ppttc/JSON workflow. Use for performance calibration, saving bridges, HC mix, labor productivity, regional benchmarks, waterfall, stacked/clustered column or bar, line, Mekko, and Gantt/timeline requests where charts must remain genuinely editable with think-cell and must not be replaced by native PowerPoint charts.

name: think-challenge
description: Challenge a design with grounded adversarial counters.

name: think-challenge
description: Use this skill when the user wants their ideas challenged with real-world counter-arguments, opposing evidence or critic perspectives found online, so the ideas become stronger. Trigger on challenge this, think-challenge, steel-man the opposition, find counter-arguments, what would critics say, stress-test this idea. Always ground counters in search results. Store lasting conclusions via Atlas remember when useful.

name: think-cheatsheet
description: Use this when the user wants to code manually but needs a fast cheatsheet of programming-language built-ins, syntax, framework APIs, or library methods based on a feature description, without receiving a full project-specific implementation.

name: think-clarifier
description: Clarify underspecified user requirements into a planning-ready brief through a stronger two-stage clarification system with stage-specific route control, delegation-aware questioning, prefill-plus-confirm question cards, route-aware Stage 2 burden control, and auditable runtime validation. Use when Codex must turn ambiguous project, feature, workflow, webpage, document, or skill requests into a controllable planning handoff while reducing user burden without weakening critical confirmation.

name: think-clarify
description: Decide what genuinely needs a human answer vs what can proceed on a sensible default. Use when a PRD, brief, or task is ambiguous in Product Builder — loaded by /pb:init and /pb:specify — to ask the few high-leverage questions and assume the rest, so building isn't blocked by over-asking or derailed by wrong guesses. Not for critiquing the requirements (use think-critique-prd) or parsing them (use ref-prd).

name: think-closed-loop
description: 思维模型：闭环。一件事要从一方转到另一方之前，先过三句：转手会丢信息，做对它要用到的写不下来的上下文多就不转；回路越紧越稳，决定后面很多步的事放在每一步都看得见的回路里；一块多大由接的一方验得完多少定。准备派子代理、把一件事交给人或另一个会话、定一程或一片多大、上下文快被压缩时加载；人说「这件事你自己做」「一块别太大」「多久看一次」，或点名 /think-closed-loop 时也加载。自己一口气做完、不转手的小活不加载。派发简报的写法与花费归 delegate-brief。

name: think-cog
description: Complex ideas need iteration, not conversation. Think → Do → Review → Repeat. CellCog completes the full loop — brainstorming, reasoning, problem-solving, strategic thinking, then executing across every modality: research, documents, visuals, data, prototypes. Like having an Alfred who doesn't just advise — he builds.

name: think-cog
description: AI thinking partner powered by CellCog. Brainstorming, reasoning, problem-solving, idea development, strategic thinking, decision support. Your collaborative thinking partner for complex problems.

name: think-commitment-variant
description: Privacy commitment-vs-implementation gap analysis. USE THIS SKILL for: commitment, promise, privacy policy, DPA, terms of service, privacy notice, implementation gap, say vs do, retention, deletion, data processing agreement. STRATEGY: Commitment Variant Analysis.

name: think-complexity-domain-sort
description: Runs a Complexity Domain Sort, sorting a situation into Clear, Complicated, Complex, Chaotic, or Confusion and choosing the response posture that fits, caveat-first. It leads with the weak evidence (the 2021 PMC internal-medicine review found scientific proof of its validity has yet to be provided), then forces the discipline the bare label lacks, namely an explicit response posture and a concrete next action rather than just a name. Use only when this complexity sort (also known as Cynefin) is asked for by name; for cause decomposition prefer think-issue-tree.

name: think-concept-mapping
description: Builds a concept map - a non-hierarchical network of concept nodes joined by directed, labeled linking phrases so each node-link-node reads as an explicit proposition, with cross-links across clusters - then surfaces gaps, missing links, and questionable propositions. Use when a domain has many interrelated concepts and the goal is to externalize and inspect how they relate, forcing every relationship to be named rather than left as a vague association.

name: think-consider-the-unknowns
description: Produces a known-unknowns ledger by enumerating the relevant evidence not in hand, the variables that bear on a judgment but are unknown or unobservable, rating each unknown by its bearing and its obtainability, then re-rating confidence against the mapped gap. Use when a consequential one-off judgment rests on thin or partial evidence, no usable base rate exists, and the confidence on the table may be inflated by what was never looked at. Not for cases with a real reference class, for widening a numeric interval, or for unknowns cheap enough to just go resolve.

name: think-consistency
description: Self-Consistency reasoning — run multiple independent reasoning paths and take consensus. Use for high-stakes decisions where reasoning errors are costly.

name: think-contradiction-resolution
description: Converts a stuck trade-off into a contradiction to dissolve rather than a compromise to settle for. Names the two conflicting requirements, states an implementation-free Ideal Final Result, and applies the four separation principles (separate the requirements in time, space, scale, or condition) to satisfy both at once, then produces either a concrete resolution or an honest flag that the trade-off is genuine. Use when a decision has hardened into an either/or like speed versus quality, thorough versus fast, or generous versus profitable, when splitting the difference feels wrong and a win-wi…

name: think-contradiction-tension-mapping
description: Produces a both/and polarity map - two interdependent poles, the upside and downside quadrant of each, a greater purpose and a deeper fear, early-warning signs, and action steps - for a chronic tension that should be managed rather than resolved. Use when an organization keeps oscillating destructively between two opposites that are both true and interdependent (centralize versus decentralize, stability versus change, candor versus diplomacy), and treating each swing as a problem to solve is the actual mistake. Not for a dissolvable trade-off and not for a real either/or choice.

name: think-core
description: Core reasoning triad — Inductive, Deductive, and Abductive. Use when the user invokes `/think inductive`, `/think deductive`, or `/think abductive`, or asks to generalize from examples, derive conclusions from rules, or find the best explanation for observations.

name: think-council
description: Power skill that runs a read-only research council with an adversarial challenge pass, so Think resolves from evidence what it can and escalates only genuine decisions.

name: think-council
description: 当用户需要多角度分析问题、深入讨论话题、验证想法、发现思维盲区、评估决策风险、审视方案时，使用此技能。自动组建多视角讨论团（通常5人），通过独立思考、基于内容的交叉讨论和结构化总结，帮助用户形成更全面的判断。触发场景包括但不限于：用户说"分析"、"讨论"、"评估"、"审视"、"不同角度"、"帮我看看这个方案"、"有什么风险"、"这个想法怎么样"、"做个决定"——即使没有明确说"讨论团"，只要任务涉及需要多视角思考的复杂问题，就应该触发。

name: think-critically

Use when user says "evaluate this prompt", "review my prompt", "will this work?", "critique this", or "check my instructions". Adversarial analysis with expectations scorecard and actionable recommendations.

name: think-critique-prd
description: Push back on a PRD or feature brief before building — surface unclear goals, missing personas, assumption gaps, unrealistic scope, and missing edge cases. Use when reviewing requirements in Product Builder — loaded by /pb:init and /pb:specify — so the prototype is built on solid intent, not silent assumptions. Not for parsing the PRD into context (use ref-prd) or deciding what to ask the user (use think-clarify).

name: think-cycle

name: think-data-journey

name: think-debug

name: think-decision-journal
description: Produces a decision journal entry that records a consequential decision at the moment it is made - the decision, the rationale, the predicted outcome, an explicit confidence level, and the assumptions it rests on - so it can be honestly reviewed later against what actually happened. Use when committing to a consequential, uncertain decision (a launch, hire, investment, bet, or strategic choice) and you want to lock in the prediction now to defeat hindsight bias and build calibration, or when pairing a record-now step with a later review.

name: think-decision-option-review
description: Produces a criteria-weighted option matrix by comparing a set of options against weighted criteria, scoring each, surfacing the explicit tradeoffs, and recommending one while flagging where the scoring is soft. Use when choosing among several real options, or when a decision needs its tradeoffs made explicit rather than left to intuition.

name: think-decision-option-review

Trigger even if the user doesn't ask you to "think hard"; trigger especially when you feel confident quickly, since fast confidence is the main failure mode this skill exists to catch.

name: think-diagnose

name: think-dialectical-bootstrapping

Use this when making a long-horizon commitment, planning under capacity constraints, setting pricing or access policy, resolving a contested default, deciding what you are…

Use this when designing a component API or design system, deciding library versus copy-in, building a CLI or registry, versioning without breaking anyone, writing for agent consumers, or building chat and streaming interfaces. name: think-like-the-user
description: Lay out interactions in the order a first-time user works, not the order the code was written: actions next to what they act on, common tasks one step away, no extra confirmations, modes or wizard steps, no features, menus or settings nobody asked for, no developer-only info on screen (tech stack, "Powered by", hook/render counts, internal IDs, paths, stack traces), good defaults and clear errors. Use when designing or changing buttons, flows, forms, dialogs, menus, settings or CLI prompts; walk the main task and count steps before calling UI work done.

description: Apply Theo's reasoning about working with generated code and evaluating the tools that produce it: stop asking how much code you should read and start asking how much you should generate, spend cheap disposable code on verifying the code that matters, convert every repeated correction into a lint rule or a CI step so it is automated forever, encode domain knowledge as infrastructure rather than leaving it in people's heads, measure the cost of finishing a task rather than the price of a unit, and change your position in public without deleting the record. Use this when deciding how much of an…

name: think-like-wangziru
description: 按王自如的思考顺序产出有结论、有原因、经得起追问的内容。用户说「用王自如 skill 分析一下…」「用王自如的方式写一篇稿子」「我想和王自如聊聊…」「王自如帮我改一下这份逐字稿」，或者要求像王自如那样分析问题、写口播、改稿、对谈时使用。不冒充本人，不编造他的经历和观点。

name: think-like-zaid
description: Apply the engineering standards used in these codebases: match a named reference product instead of inventing a look, verify in the running app rather than the diff, delete features instead of complicating them, fix the mechanism rather than the symptom, and treat AI-slop design and unverified claims as defects. Use this when deciding UI direction, choosing a stack, cutting scope, reviewing a plan before code exists, or checking finished work against the quality bar. Reach for it before proposing architecture or design in these codebases, even when the skill is never named.

name: think-like-zerox
description: Zerox's personal meta skill for conversations and development work. Challenge assumptions, grill unclear ideas, and guide substantial changes through specs, plans, tasks, tests, implementation, and OCR delegation review. Use as Zerox's default working style, scaling the workflow to the request; ordinary questions need a direct answer rather than development artifacts.

name: think-linear-model-aggregation
description: Builds a simple mechanical scoring model - a few weighted predictive cues combined by a fixed formula and applied consistently - for a repeated predictive judgment, because consistent simple rules reliably match or beat holistic expert intuition. Use when the same kind of evaluative judgment recurs (screening candidates, scoring leads, triaging) and gut calls are inconsistent or overconfident.

name: think-logic
description: Define the behavior of a Product Builder screen or component — states, transitions, validation rules, and conditional rendering. Use when adding interactivity or logic — loaded by /pb:build when logic changes. Maps intent onto the shell's declarative data-* runtime (data-required, data-validate, data-action="submit", data-go, etc.). Not for arranging elements (use think-layout) or connecting whole screens into a journey (use craft-connect-flow).

name: think-mathematics
description: Mathematical, physical, and computational reasoning methods — Mathematics (proofs, algebra, calculus), Physics (tensors, conservation laws, symmetries), and Computability (Turing machines, decidability, complexity classes). Use when the user invokes `/think mathematics`, `/think physics`, or `/think computability`, or asks about formal proofs, physical models, or computability/complexity questions.

name: think-minimax-regret
description: Produces a regret (opportunity-loss) matrix with the minimax pick and the binding worst-case state, choosing among options over un-probabilized states of nature. Use when a few discrete options face a few discrete uncontrollable states and no defensible probabilities exist. Not an expected-value tree (which needs probabilities) and not an attribute scorecard.

name: think-mode
description: Decision helper for picking the right read-only opencode workflow — researcher, debate, one-shot solution-brief, or phased solution-brief (research.md → debate.md → brief.md) — based on the question's uncertainty shape. Use this when the operator asks "should we research / debate / solution-brief this?", before drafting any new read-only session prompt, when the framing is ambiguous about which workflow shape fits, or when a stakeholder reframe has just landed and the workflow choice should be reconsidered.

name: think-model-first
description: 思维模型：建模先于代码。写碰到状态与操作的代码之前，先把每个操作写成偏函数，写明它在哪些前置状态下有定义；再全化，定义域之外的每一格给一个确定的答复，不变式排除的格写不可达；最后翻成领域模型与对象模型再写代码，每个类型能指回模型。设计或实现会话、任务、连接、资源这类有生灭的对象，加一个操作或一个状态，或实现里出现「不该发生」的分支时加载；人说「先建模」「全化一下」「状态表呢」，或点名 /think-model-first 时也加载。不碰状态的纯计算与纯文档改动不加载。

name: think-morphological-analysis
description: Produces a morphological field (a Zwicky box of independent parameters by their possible values) plus a cross-consistency-pruned set of internally consistent configurations. Use when a solution is genuinely a configuration - a choice on each of several semi-independent dimensions (product architecture, service bundle, policy package) - and the risk is defaulting to one familiar combination and never seeing the rest of the space. Not a top-down MECE tree and not a provoked option list.

name: think-natural-frequency-bayesian
description: Converts a conditional-probability or base-rate question into natural frequencies over a concrete population (for example 9 of 1000) to compute the correct posterior and expose base-rate neglect, and refuses to proceed without real input rates. Use when interpreting a test result, screening signal, or any "given a positive, what is the real probability" question.

name: think-of-ai-as-a-junior-assistant
description: Delegate a bounded task with context and acceptance criteria, then review the result before relying on it.

name: think-of-something-to-fix
description: Come up with good ideas about what to fix. Use when you have to fix something, but you're not sure what.

name: think-one-way-vs-two-way-door
description: Produces a reversibility classification that triages a decision before any analysis - labeling it a reversible two-way door or a hard-to-reverse one-way door - and matches the deliberation and sign-off level to that verdict, so reversible calls are made fast and irreversible ones get real rigor. Use when it is unclear how much process a decision deserves, when a team is about to rubber-stamp something irreversible or convene a committee over something trivially reversible, or when a chronically slow org needs a defensible reason to move fast or slow down.

name: think-orthogonal
description: 思维模型：正交、分形、矩阵。列清单、拆设计、划边界或定位一类反复出现的问题之前，先拆出独立变化的轴，每条轴归一个拥有者；把轴交叉成表逐格看，每格要么有答案要么写明不适用；再问这个结构在大一层和小一层是不是同一个，是就只设计一次。凭感觉列清单、同一个判断在两处各写一遍、一个概念的状态在决定另一个领域的事、特例越补越多时加载；人说「先找轴」「拆成矩阵」「这是同一个结构」，或点名 /think-orthogonal 时也加载。只有一个量在变、没有可拆的不加载。

name: think-ought-vs-is
description: 思维模型：应然与实然。做设计、实现、优化、重构、定位问题，或准备把一件事交给人定之前，先答三问：它应该是什么样，它现在是什么样，两者差在哪；差异就是全部工作。开始一项设计或一个切片、同一类问题第二次出现、一件事做得比预计久、准备重跑贵的命令找原因时加载；人说「先写应然」「本质解」「别缝缝补补」，或点名 /think-ought-vs-is 时也加载。只查一个已知事实不加载。

name: think-pairwise-comparison
description: Produces a binary-vote comparison matrix (every pair judged A-beats-B), a derived ranking, and a consistency check, ordering options without any criteria axis or absolute scoring. Use when items must be ranked but no defensible scale or articulable criteria exist. Not a criteria-weighted option matrix and not a base-rate forecast.

name: think-parallel
description: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies

name: think-parallel-perspectives-review
description: Evaluates a decision or idea through several deliberately separated lenses in turn (facts, upside, risks, intuition, alternatives, process) so that no single mode dominates, then synthesizes them into a balanced read, producing a multi-lens review. Use when a choice needs a rounded look, or when risk-aversion or optimism is drowning out the other perspectives.

name: think-plan

name: think-pose
description: Holds a thinking pose, resting the chin on one hand with the other arm supporting the elbow and the gaze drifting upward. Use when the command mentions think, thinking, ponder, hmm, contemplate, or the thinker pose.

name: think-premortem
description: Generates a ranked risk register that stress-tests a planned decision by imagining it has already failed, surfacing the likely causes and pairing each with a mitigation, tripwire, and kill criterion. Use when about to commit to a launch, hire, investment, migration, or any risky, hard-to-reverse decision, or when you need risks surfaced before committing.

name: think-premortem
description: Pre-mortem for a plan, decision, or running system. Plan mode imagines how a plan fails; scenario mode investigates a posed catastrophe against the actual code. Produces a prioritized risk register with early-warning signals. Feedback only.

name: think-premortem
description: 在尚能调整的重要计划开始前，假设计划已失败，倒推具体原因，并把主要风险转成预警、预防动作和暂停条件；不用于已经发生的失败复盘或琐碎选择。

STRATEGY: Privacy Adversarial.

Use when the user invokes `/think bayesian` or `/think evidential`, or asks about updating beliefs with evidence, computing posterior probabilities, weighing multi-source evidence, or probabilistic inference under uncertainty.

name: think-problem-restatement
description: Generates several genuinely different framings of an ambiguous problem by varying altitude, stakeholder, and goal-versus-implementation, then selects the most useful one to solve and produces a reframed problem statement with How Might We angles. Use when a problem is vague, arrived as a symptom or a pre-baked solution, or before committing significant work to solving the wrong thing.

name: think-process-tracing
description: Evaluates rival causal explanations of a single case by typing each piece of within-case evidence by its diagnosticity (hoop, smoking-gun, straw-in-the-wind, doubly-decisive tests) against each rival's mechanism chain, then eliminating or confirming rivals item by item rather than by tallying. Use when one outcome has happened, several genuine rival explanations compete to explain it, and mechanism-level evidence (logs, timestamps, documents, who knew what when) is available to discriminate them - an incident postmortem, a churn spike, a lost deal, a metric anomaly. Not for cross-case general…

name: think-pyramid-principle
description: Produces a pyramid that structures a recommendation answer-first - a single governing thought on top, a small set of MECE, deliberately ordered key arguments beneath it, and supporting evidence under each (Minto), with an optional SCQA intro framing. Use when a conclusion or recommendation already exists and must be communicated clearly to a busy or senior reader, when findings need to be ordered into a tight top-down case, or when a write-up buries its point under context.

name: think-python-2e
description: Knowledge from the book "Think Python 2e": The way of the program; Variables, expressions and statements; Functions; Case study: interface design; Conditionals and recursion; Fruitful functions; Iteration; Strings; Case study: word play; Lists; Dictionaries; Tuples; Case study: data structure selection; Files; Classes and objects; Classes and functions; Classes and methods; Inheritance; The Goodies; Debugging; Analysis of Algorithms. Use when a task needs the book's definitions, explanations or worked examples on these topics.

name: think-qualitative-comparative-analysis
description: Handles a by-name request for QCA (Qualitative Comparative Analysis), the truth-table-and-Boolean-minimization method, honestly. At session scale the input almost never exists and the method certifies configurations from noise, so this skill does NOT build the truth table as if valid. It leads with that evidence, then routes to the evidence-based move the job actually needs (think-reference-class-forecasting for a set of comparable cases, or think-process-tracing for a single case). Use only when someone asks for QCA or a truth-table minimization by name.

name: think-question-burst
description: Generates a rapid burst of questions about a problem (questions only, no answers), then ranks them for which would most change the approach and selects the single most catalytic one to pursue, producing a ranked question set. Use when you are stuck, too attached to one framing, or need a better question before answering.

Trigger on ramble, think-ramble, brain dump, random ideas, capture this, store these thoughts, I’m just thinking out loud. Routes storage through Atlas remember when a store is present.

name: think-random-frameworks
description: Generates three off-pattern framework analyses of a topic by drawing frameworks at random, applying each regardless of fit, and harvesting the non-obvious angles the unexpected lenses expose. Use when a framing feels frozen or fixated and the goal is to break out of it with deliberately unranked methods rather than the obvious best-fit ones. Use when relevance-ranked selection would only reinforce the stuck view and a random draw is wanted to surface what a fitted analysis would miss.

name: think-react
description: ReAct reasoning — explicit reason-act-observe cycle for investigation and debugging. Use when you need to interleave reasoning with tool actions systematically.

name: think-red-team-light
description: Produces an adversarial critique by constructing the strongest case against a proposal or thesis (the best objections an intelligent adversary would raise), then judging which objections actually land and what would rebut them. Use when a plan has too-easy consensus and needs pressure-testing, or to steelman the opposition before committing.

name: think-reference-class-forecasting
description: Produces a reference-class estimate by defining a class of similar past cases, taking their base-rate distribution of outcomes, and anchoring the forecast on that outside view rather than the optimistic inside view, with a conservative adjustment for specifics. Use when forecasting cost, time, or odds of success for a project prone to optimism or the planning fallacy.

Takes a project, incident, decision that played out, or time period; gathers ground truth (observations) separately from recollections; spawns reflectors applying different lenses (what-worked-vs-got-lucky, what-didn't, what-surprised, system-rewards-vs-intent, decisions-that-aged, what-to-tell-past-self, patterns-that-recur) in isolation; synthesizes into updated mental models as first-class output. Produces feedback only — no code, no tickets, no artifacts.

name: think-reflective-equilibrium
description: Runs reflective equilibrium (mutual adjustment between considered case judgments, general principles, and background theories) caveat-first. It leads with the weak evidence (philosophically central since Rawls 1971 but empirically untested as a procedure, with three failure modes that bite in a bounded session), then forces the discipline a bare run lacks, namely an explicit revision ledger that records which commitment gave way and why. Use only when reflective equilibrium is asked for by name; for impartial allocation prefer think-veil-of-ignorance-reasoning, for a parties-by-principles aud…

Takes a stated problem, extracts its premises, then spawns reframers applying different lenses (problem-vs-symptom, scope-shift, stakeholder-shift, level-of-abstraction, time-horizon, inversion, category-shift, constraints-shift) in isolation, and synthesizes the alternatives into a report with an orchestrator recommendation. Produces feedback only — no code, no tickets, no artifacts.

name: think-REPLACE-method
description: REPLACE with one sentence. Lead with an action verb (Generates / Produces / Evaluates / Audits / Checks), name the artifact it produces, and include a "Use when ..." clause with concrete trigger words. Third person. Do NOT use first person ("you can", "you should", "we "). Keep under 1024 characters. This text is the activation trigger and is scored by the toolkit (U5).

name: think-research-framework
description: Researches a thinking framework end to end and produces a schema-valid proposed registry entry plus a learning dossier, grading the evidence on the seven-tier model and assessing overlap against the shipped catalog. Use when you need an honest evidence grade and a build-or-fold verdict for a candidate method before turning it into a skill, when reproducing the evidence-and-overlap vetting on a method the catalog already judged, or when you need a ranked shortlist of new candidate methods in a family.

name: think-review-ask
description: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements

name: think-review-take
description: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation

name: think-right-reasoning-allocation-calibration
description: Dynamically allocate reasoning budgets per-task: 36.8% length reduction while improving accuracy 8.4% by learning which problems warrant deep reasoning vs. quick answers. Use when optimizing reasoning efficiency across variable-difficulty problems.

name: think-right-then-well
description: 思维模型：先做对，再做好。写代码分两轮：做对只求验收标准逐条过、测试先红后绿，不打磨；做好一轮不加能力，只改实现；好不好由结构读数、差分变异和一份品味核对单判，核对单每问指到代码位置作答。开始实现一个切片或一个修复、做对之后准备收口、发现自己一边找正确一边打磨时加载；人说「先做对」「做好一轮」「品味呢」，或点名 /think-right-then-well 时也加载。只改文档、不写代码不加载。

name: think-rigorously
description: First-person rigor patterns for non-trivial work — type/dimension check, decompose, bound-then-refine, sanity at limits, falsifiability. Use before starting a derivation, proof, training run, or analysis, and again when stuck. Sister to /scientific-critical-thinking (about others' claims) and /hypothesis-generation (structured ideation); this one runs on your own working before claims solidify.

name: think-role-boundary
description: Controller/Processor/Sub-processor boundary analysis for privacy risk discovery. USE THIS SKILL for: controller, processor, sub-processor, data role, role boundary, organizational boundary, jurisdiction, cross-border, DPA, data processing agreement. STRATEGY: Role & Boundary Analysis.

name: think-role-storming
description: Produces a persona-tagged divergent idea list, ideas generated while inhabiting a chosen non-self identity to lower self-censorship and shift associations. Use when idea flow is throttled by self-consciousness or a fixated frame rather than missing knowledge, and you want more and stranger candidates before converging. Not evaluation through fixed lenses (that is parallel-perspectives) and not genuine challenge (that is authentic-dissent).

name: think-router
description: Unified router for reasoning, research, and analysis tasks. Consolidates reasoning-router + research-router + analysis-router.

name: think-router-hybrid-reasoning
description: Route reasoning between discrete token space (when uncertain) and latent soft embeddings (when confident). Use maximum next-token probability as a routing threshold to dynamically select the reasoning space, improving accuracy under latent reasoning while reducing computational cost through selective discrete sampling.

name: think-scamper
description: Generates a structured set of variations on an existing idea, product, or process by running it through seven transformation prompts (substitute, combine, adapt, modify, put to other use, eliminate, reverse), then shortlists the most promising, producing an expansion sheet. Use when you have a seed idea and need to break past the obvious options; not for blank-page ideation.

name: think-scenario-planning
description: Produces a scenario set, 2-4 contrasting and internally consistent short narratives of alternative external futures named by two critical-uncertainty axes, plus a robustness read of the strategy across the worlds (which moves survive every world, which early signals show which world is arriving, which options to keep open). Use when the planning horizon is long and the decisive forces are outside control and not reliably predictable, and a single implicit forecast is driving the strategy. Not forecasting and not a single preferred path.

name: think-scientific
description: Scientific and structural reasoning methods — Scientific Method (hypothesis formation, experiment design, falsifiability), Systems Thinking (feedback loops, 8 systems archetypes, leverage points), and Formal Logic (propositional/predicate logic, formal proofs, soundness). Use when the user invokes `/think scientificmethod`, `/think systemsthinking`, or `/think formallogic`, or asks about experiment design, systemic behavior, or formal logical proofs.

description: Good-faith adversarial scrutiny of an idea or plan. Spawns critical skeptics across relevant lenses, pairs them with an advocate defending the idea, and synthesizes the exchange into a report. Produces feedback only — no code, no tickets, no artifacts.

description: 实验系统研究（查询引擎与数据系统、存储、运行时、分布式与机器学习系统）的工作方法与思考框架：第一性原理分解、自顶向下的问题刻画、自底向上逐层求解，以及快速的假设—实现—评估循环。每当任务是规划、实现、测量、优化、比较或报告一个系统的性能、内存、可扩展性或效率，或者是运行一个实验系列时，就使用它，包括「刻画」「瓶颈」「为什么慢」「基线」「消融」「阶梯」「对数据集抽样」「这次运行太久」「在规模上还成立吗」「这值得试吗」「下一步是什么」「写步骤记录」「报告结果」。当一次会话滑向等待、反复验证、旁支、以预测的运行结果代替假设，或数字含糊时，也使用它。即使用户没有点名任何方法，也应用它。

name: think-sharp
description: Working method and thinking framework for experimental systems research (query engines and data systems, storage, runtimes, distributed and ML systems): first-principles decomposition, top-down problem characterization, bottom-up solution layer by layer, and a fast assumption-implementation-evaluation loop. Use it whenever the task is to plan, implement, measure, optimize, compare or report on a system's performance, memory, scalability or efficiency, or to run an experiment campaign, including 'characterize', 'bottleneck', 'why is it slow', 'baseline', 'ablation', 'ladder', 'sample the datas…

description: Produces an anti-goals register by assuming a design succeeds at scale, narrating the near-future in which that success harms third parties (including non-users) and is exploited in bad faith by named bad actors, then converting each speculated harm into a standing design constraint bound into the requirements. Use when a feature's success case could externalize harm onto people outside the customer relationship (location, ranking, inference, targeting, automation) and the team's risk review is entirely project-centric. Not a premortem (route plan-survival risk there), not for present documen…

name: think-standard

description: Install or diagnose ThinkWeave under Codex, especially on native Windows when weave is missing, resolves but cannot import, or is blocked by the sandbox.
