One Bash call (`weave health --json`), a handful of weave_* retrievals, judgment narration, one `weave_create` (the next watermark). Pull-only, user-invoked; flags digest/cron failures at consumption, never heals them unasked.

name: thinkweave-capture
description: Inline-text ingestion (snippet, quote, brief, fragment) — classify content shape, propose source_type, create a `note` (or `source` when applicable) via `weave_create` with ontology-aligned concepts. Called from `/ingest` for the inline-text shape.

name: thinkweave-discover
description: Strategy-driven discovery. Runs the configured strategy list; strategies emit gap descriptors and (for external-trigger ones) directly enqueue. The single producer rail in the discover→drain spine.

name: thinkweave-drain
description: Drain a per-source-type acquisition queue. Source-type-agnostic — config in `vault/config/sources.yaml` decides whether items dispatch to a per-type research skill (sequential) or fan out to subagents (parallel).

name: thinkweave-dream
description: Periodic dream cycle — two-phase subagent orchestrator. Phase 1 fans out 5 synthesis workers (promotion/merge/theme/essence/priority), merges plan fragments, applies. Phase 2 fans out 5 composition workers (wrap catch-up, prediction judge, hub seam-link, memory seam, knowledge digest). One cron entry, ten workers, single maintenance.jsonl line per cycle. Owns routine ontology dedup for BOTH hub families (drift v2: cosine + verdict memory) AND CC-auto-memory↔vault reconciliation (the memory seam). Self-deciding, headless-safe.

name: thinkweave-explain
description: One-shot explainer — `/explain` (the current session's knowledge) or `/explain diff [ref | #pr]` (one code change). Writes a `kind: explain` note in the session folder, optionally with an HTML explainer beside it; a re-run on the same target updates that note. Ends with non-blocking check questions. Never prompts.

name: thinkweave-hubs-link

name: thinkweave-import-chatgpt
description: Inline ChatGPT-export import — walk conversations.json, summarize each thread via the running model, and weave_create one note per conversation. The `weave import chatgpt --via inline` path; pairs with `--via batch` which fans out via the API wrapper instead.

name: thinkweave-ingest
description: Universal input router — classifies input shape (URL / file / text / structured-id) and dispatches to the appropriate ingestion skill. The single user-facing front door for getting external content into the vault.

name: thinkweave-ingest-paper-file
description: Local PDF paper ingestion — extract text, derive title/authors, detect arxiv ID, write a `source_type: paper` note with the PDF and extracted text staged as companions. Called from `/ingest` for the local-PDF file shape.

name: thinkweave-judge-prediction
description: Evaluate one or more decisions' predicted_outcome against current vault + filesystem evidence. Appends a {match, judged_at, reason} entry to each decision's prediction_history. Self-contained; headless-safe.

name: thinkweave-learn
description: Vault-grounded tutor — `/learn <topic>`. Teach-then-test dialogue; the vault is the syllabus, the user's own learning history is the spine, a capped acquisition fill covers gaps, the transcript is the comprehension evidence. One learn note per session. Interactive by nature (not headless).

name: thinkweave-news
description: One-off URL ingest for news articles, mid-conversation. Dispatches a Sonnet writer directly; no triage gate (you've already decided this is worth briefing).

name: thinkweave-newsletter
description: Orchestrator over the email-newsletter intake rails. Probes the Gmail connector, reads the per-type `mail_poll` discover-strategy plan (effective_query + processed_label), fetches threads via Gmail MCP, enqueues, drains, then applies the processed_label. Headless-safe.

name: thinkweave-onboard
description: First-run onboarding — pre-flight checks, vault wiring, seed vault from prior Claude Code history, bootstrap ontology, configure focus + sources (validated against user-supplied sample files), install hooks (global by default), optionally install cron block, run end-to-end smoke test, emit landing docs.

name: thinkweave-podcast

name: thinkweave-recall
description: Explicit, read-only ThinkWeave recall workflow. Use only when the user invokes `$thinkweave-recall` or explicitly asks to use the recall skill. For ordinary history or context questions, call the available `weave_*` tools directly without loading this skill.

name: thinkweave-research

name: thinkweave-research-podcast
description: Resolve a single pasted podcast RSS-feed URL into a queue item for its latest episode and drain one `research-podcast-worker`. Called from `/research` (router). The one-shot analog of `/podcast`'s discover+drain.

name: thinkweave-research-repo
description: Fetch a GitHub / GitLab repo, extract architectural summary + key files, write it as a `source_type: repo` note. Called from `/research` (router) or `/drain --source-type repo`.

name: thinkweave-research-youtube
description: Resolve a single pasted YouTube URL into a queue item and drain one `research-youtube-worker`. Called from `/research` (router). The one-shot analog of `/youtube`'s discover+drain — same two rails, one video.

name: thinkweave-seed-enrich

The keyless `--via inline` half of `weave import {claude-code|codex} --enrich`; pairs with `--via batch` which fans out through the API wrapper.

name: thinkweave-source-fit
description: Read-only diagnostic — given a free-form description of an input shape, classify it against existing source types. Returns covered / adapt / scaffold.

name: thinkweave-source-scaffold
description: Generative wizard — register a new source type via vault overlay + machine-global skill file. No repo edits.

name: thinkweave-substack
description: Drain the Substack disk inbox (browser-clipped posts) into the vault. Figure-aware via multimodal Read; archives processed bundles.

name: thinkweave-tighten

One process; the nightly /dream runs the same mechanism unattended.

name: thinkweave-update-hubs
description: Concept-hub sync — incremental (default) for daily deltas, or `--bulk [inline|batch]` for backfill on fresh / long-untended vaults.

name: thinkweave-wrap
description: End-of-session memory extraction. Compose insights/decisions inline, call `weave_extract` once, then `weave wrap-finalize` (deterministic tail). Self-contained; never prompts the user.

name: thinkweave-youtube
description: Thin orchestrator over the YouTube intake rails. Calls the `rss_poll` discover strategy to enqueue from channel RSS feeds, then `/drain --source-type youtube-*` to fan out writer subagents. Headless-safe.

name: thinkwise-sf-deployment
description: Reference guide for starting, monitoring, and controlling a Thinkwise Software Factory definition-generation job — generating the application definition alone, or the full generate/validate/build/deploy pipeline ("complete creation"). Use whenever an MCP connector with Software Factory access starts, checks, cancels, or resolves a paused step of a generation/validation/deployment job.

name: thinkwise-sf-icons

Use whenever an MCP connector with Software Factory access creates, inspects, reuses, replaces, or assigns an icon.

name: thinkwise-sf-maps

name: thinkwise-sf-menus

name: tk-repository-guidance
description: [user/auto] 저장소 맥락·도메인 문서·외부 계약의 조사 기준을 참조할 때 사용합니다. 실제 업무 실행이나 변경 권한을 부여하지 않습니다.

name: tk-research
description: Use to investigate unknowns before planning a large change: give bounded library, API, prior-art and pitfalls questions to one source-qualified research owner, then consolidate evidence, contradictions and unknowns into RESEARCH.md.

name: tk-research
description: [user/auto] 외부 선행 사례·접근법 비교, 스킬·워크플로 증류 제안, 지속 연구와 재개에 사용합니다. 배경·근거·한계를 대화로 보고하며 HTML 등 산출물은 요청한 경우에 만듭니다. 스킬 정본 수정이나 제품 구현은 담당하지 않습니다.

name: tk-research
description: Trend research TikTok via Perplexity sonar-deep-research + FireCrawl scraping. Accumule des sessions de recherche dans la DB, genere un BRIEF.md consolide. Utiliser avant de creer du contenu pour identifier les tendances et hooks qui marchent dans la niche freelances/CRM/SaaS.

name: tk-restore
description: Use when recovering context or exporting verified backups.

name: tk-retro
description: [user/auto] 현재 또는 지정한 코딩 세션의 실행 과정·반복 실수·도구 낭비를 회고하거나, 관찰된 Agent Skill 장애의 원인을 조사하고 재발 방지 개선안을 제안합니다. 일반 코드 리뷰, 정적 스킬 카탈로그 감사, 직접 구현에는 사용하지 않습니다.

name: tk-review
description: Use for independent cross-family review of a plan before execution or a completed diff: preserve selected reviewers, consolidate evidence-backed findings and disagreements, and block approval on insufficient actual families, stale targets, unresolved blocker or major findings, or missing verification.

name: tk-review
description: [user/auto] 특정 PR·커밋 범위·현재 worktree를 리뷰하거나 변경의 Spec/AC·품질을 독립 판정해 달라는 명확한 요청에 사용합니다. 대상이 특정되지 않은 일반 코드 질문, 구현·수정·발행에는 사용하지 않습니다.

name: tk-rewrite
description: [user/auto] 기존 답변이나 문서가 이해하기 어렵거나, 배경을 모르는 독자에게 공유하거나, 한국어 AI 말투와 번역투를 다듬을 때 사용합니다. 세션 현황 조회, 새 시각 설명 자료 제작, 코드 수정에는 사용하지 않습니다.

name: tk-roadmap
description: [user/auto] 목표와 기술·비기술 제약을 바탕으로 추진 방향, 우선순위·마일스톤이 있는 로드맵을 수립해 달라는 명확한 자연어 요청에 사용합니다. 구체적인 구현 준비, 단순 일정 질문, 기존 계획의 전면 감사에는 사용하지 않습니다.

name: tk-route-mode
description: [user] 위임 능력 티어별 모델과 effort의 기본 및 절약 모드를 확인·전환하거나 사용자 모드를 추가·갱신하고, 현재 호스트의 사용자 수준 에이전트 설정을 승인받아 적용·검증·복원할 때 사용합니다. 개별 작업의 티어 선택이나 메인 세션 모델 변경에는 사용하지 않습니다.

name: tk-router
description: Use when starting big-repo multi-model work: sizes the change, has you pick three model classes (one planner, a set of executors, reviewers) from the local catalog, checks which workflow backend and sibling tk-* stages are actually available, and routes through the thunderkit lifecycle with plan review gated before execution. Entry point for the thunderkit pack.

name: tk-seed
description: Seed a session for one unit of trapperkeeper work -- classify the sources by provenance, load the unit's context, shape each of its issues, put their design choices to the owner, and write the seed report. Loaded by tk-start and tk-start-next after they have fixed the unit; never invoked by the owner.

name: tk-setup
description: Configure a repo for the tk-* workflow skills: layout, docs paths, module codes, verify commands. Run once per repo.

name: tk-setup-skills
description: [user] TigerKit 스킬 선택 설치 계획이나 누락된 참조 의존성 확인을 명시적으로 요청할 때 사용합니다. 설치·설정 변경은 별도 승인 후 수행하며 일반 스킬 실행 중 자동 설치하거나 자동 호출하지 않습니다.

name: tk-ship
description: Use when a completed change needs a readiness check and PR-body draft: require fresh cross-family review, per-lane verification, applicable UAT and unchanged frozen paths; prepare an engineering summary and branch handoff only, without push, PR creation, merge, deploy or publication.

name: tk-signoff
description: Stage [4] of the tk workflow: trace every requirement through plan, code, tests and verification, decide Go / No-Go, and on Go append the intent Outcome, update module specs, move the intent to the intents folder under its ID and delete only the selected task's temporary artifacts without asking; the human commits after signoff. Use when the user runs it or tk-workflow routes to it.

name: tk-skill-vet
description: [user/auto] 외부 Agent Skill이나 plugin을 설치하기 전, 또는 업데이트의 새 동작을 정적으로 보안 검토합니다. 기존 스킬의 중복·낡은 지침 감사나 실제 설치는 담당하지 않습니다.

name: tk-slides
description: Generation de slides TikTok via multi-provider (Gemini principal, OpenAI/Stability/ Replicate/Pollinations en fallback). Gere le rate limiting Gemini free-tier, le resume-on-failure, et la detection de quota quotidien. Utiliser pour generer ou debugger les slides d'un carousel.

name: tk-spec
description: Use to clarify WHAT a big change delivers before planning: runs a bounded Socratic loop over scope, interfaces, data, done-criteria and edge cases until the ambiguity gate passes, then writes a requirements-only SPEC.md that tk-plan builds on. Reuses a compatible native interview component for open questions only; never plans, executes or approves anything.

name: tk-start
description: Seed a session -- acknowledge the trapperkeeper workflow, load context for a task the owner describes or for issues the owner names, and put its design choices to the owner without starting it; for an issue already in flight, report its stage instead

name: tk-start-next
description: Seed a session with the next unit of work -- read the active milestone's goals against the tree and the open issues, closing it and moving on when the tree meets them, cut what is still missing into right-sized issues, ask the owner which to tackle together, then load their context and put their design choices to the owner without starting them

name: tk-studio-activate
description: Studio activation front door — health/drift check proving the BMad base, the studio plugin, the per-user store, and the vault window are current. Read-only, loud, guided fixes. Use when the user says "activate the studio", "tk activate", "studio status", or "check for drift".

name: tk-studio-base-update
description: Adopt a new upstream BMad release as one reviewable motion — bump the bmad.lock pin, rerun the upstream installer, open the integration PR. Use when the user says "base update", "bump bmad", "update the base", or "adopt the new BMad release".

name: tk-studio-consolidate
description: Consolidate merged measurement data into the living issues ledger — cluster defect-shaped events, mint stable ISS-NNN entries with severity, expected-vs-actual, named evidence, and fix candidates, updating rows in place. Use when the user says "consolidate the measurements", "tk consolidate", or a job's invoke-skill directive names this skill.

name: tk-studio-detect
description: Read-only recommendation inputs — inventory the full resource universe (installed BMad modules/skills, known-but-uninstalled official modules, user-authored resources) and detect what a project is with evidence. Use when the user says "inventory resources", "tk detect", "what's installed", or as the input step of onboarding.

name: tk-studio-engage
description: The planner leg of an engagement — `reply` reads the engagement's memory (the record, the chat so far, the plan under `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/`, `kb/` and `kb/confluence/`) and writes the planner's reply line, with optional proposals the owner can press, to the engagement's `chat.jsonl`; `questions` writes at most three multiple-choice clarifying questions, each with a default, for the owner's inbox; `scope` writes and publishes the scope of work; `quote` prices the scope as a seeded 50/85/95 band with a hard cap from the studio's own history and proposes `go`; `closeout` (run by the…

name: tk-studio-evals
description: The plugin's eval runner on the sandbox tier (Story 35.5, hole 85) — runs `claude plugin eval` for the eval cases the host cannot run (they need a shell and the repository tree), writes each case's result and a scores.json, and ends with the per-case passes in the status block. Driven headless by the shipped `maintenance-evals` job; use when the payload names eval `cases`, or the user says "run the plugin evals on the sandbox".

name: tk-studio-evolve
description: Evolve loop, drafting half — cluster merged observation events into the living proposals ledger, minting stable PROP-NNN rows with impact, named evidence, extracted candidate changes, and issues-ledger cross-links, updating rows in place. Drafts documents only; never applies a change. Use when the user says "draft proposals", "tk evolve", or a job's invoke-skill directive names this skill.

name: tk-studio-install
description: Install the BMad base at the committed bmad.lock pin with the project's module set — non-interactive, deterministic, zero forks. Use when the user says "tk install", "install the base", or "install bmad at the pin".

name: tk-studio-job
description: Run declared jobs on the harness's own scheduling primitives — submit, status, cancel, and wake per the driver contract, with budget guards and stop conditions enforced. Use when the user says "submit a job", "tk job", "job status", "cancel that job", or wants recurring/unattended work scheduled.

name: tk-studio-knowledge
description: The knowledge promotion gate — draft reconciled corrections from the routing doc into ordinary kb/ files on a feature branch behind a membrane PR; review is the gate, nothing auto-applies. Use when the user says "promote the corrections", "tk promote", "draft the promotion", "promote-draft", or a job's invoke-skill directive names this skill.

name: tk-studio-launch
description: Launch, inspect, or stop the execution substrate (bmad-loop) for one project epic through the studio — distill the epic's SPEC, bootstrap the first story's task manifest at the planner tier, then start the engine detached with a pre-minted run id. Use when the user says "launch epic N", "tk launch", "start the run for this epic", "run status", "stop the run", or a `run-epic` job's invoke-skill directive names this skill.

name: tk-studio-measure-push
description: Push the local measurement ledger into the shared repo as a membrane PR — feature branch, per-user-per-machine file, sanitization re-check pre-commit, review as the gate. Use when the user says "push my measurements", "tk measure push", or a job's invoke-skill directive names this skill.

name: tk-studio-migrate
description: Designed migration of a project's planning binding to Jira — closed inventory, export→transform→import→verification, copy-then-verify-then-flag cutover, source retained read-only until explicit operator clearance (AD-16). Use when the user says "migrate planning to jira", "rebind to jira", "tk migrate", or asks to move the project's backlog into the team's tracker.

name: tk-studio-observe
description: Evolve loop, v1 half — record observed toil, retrospective signals, and research findings as observation measurement events. Observe and log only; never drafts proposals. Use when the user says "log an observation", "tk observe", "note this toil", or after a retrospective surfaces a repeated manual step.

name: tk-studio-onboard
description: Onboard a project into the studio — stand up the taxonomy (store, config, registry, kb, vault window), then propose a role × project working set with evidence and record it only on explicit confirmation. Use when the user says "onboard this project", "tk onboard", "set up the studio here", or "recommend a working set".

name: tk-studio-orchestrator
description: The studio's front door — resolve who you are (role, per-user store), what this project needs (confirmed working_set.<role>), and route to resources by name, statelessly. Use when the user says "enter the studio", "tk studio", "orchestrate", "convene the council", or asks what to work on through the studio.

name: tk-studio-plan-sync
description: Planning adapter — canonicalize BMad-native planning artifacts (normalize pass, sole id authority) and sync them with the bound planning backend. Use when the user says "sync the plan", "normalize planning artifacts", "tk plan sync", or after stock BMad planning flows produce or change epics/stories.

name: tstack
description: Router and contract for tstack, which runs each engineering task through a lead the human talks to directly, with workers under it. Use for /tstack, $tstack, /skill:tstack, or a launch block that names you a tstack lead or worker.

name: tstack-architect
description: Use when a change is big enough that writing code first would fix the wrong shape: a new module, a new data model, a change to who owns some state, or a card whose design the owner must see. Sketch the caller's usage, the types and the signatures first, compare at least two shapes, put the chosen sketch on the card or a doc, then build against it and scrap it when it keeps fighting you. Skip for a one-file fix with an obvious shape (just build it, with tstack-tdd), and for comparing finished candidates (use tstack-arena).

name: tstack-arena
description: Use when one attempt at a non-trivial piece of work would fix the wrong shape: a contested design, an API, a tricky algorithm, a page of copy. Run two to four independent candidates on the same brief, have a separate judge score them against a written rubric, pick one as the base, graft the best parts of the others into it by hand, and verify the result. Covers the brief, the rubric, the judge and the synthesis note on the card. Skip for work with one obvious answer, and for splitting work into slices (use tstack-swarm).

name: tstack-babysit-pr
description: Monitor a pull request through review and CI. Use when the user asks to monitor, watch, or babysit a PR.

name: tstack-babysit-pr-2

name: tstack-benchmark-checklist
description: Use before you report or act on a performance number you measured: a speedup or regression in a PR, a CI step's time, a job's duration, a choice between two libraries or settings. Seven questions to answer with evidence from runs: what limits it, was each side tuned, does it break physical limits, did it error, does it repeat, does it matter end to end, and did the work happen at all. Covers how to state the number on a card. Skip for numbers you didn't measure, and for finding the slow code in the first place (use tstack-how, then measure).

name: tstack-brief
description: Use when the owner asks for a briefing or a mission reaches a milestone, and you, the PM, write where things stand: one plain paragraph first, then Live, In progress and Waiting on you (each ask linked, with your recommendation), and "Nothing needs you" when that is true. Covers sfora post --draft, reading it back, publishing once, correcting with a follow-up post, and a running dashboard kept as one doc updated with sfora put. Skip for card-level evidence (use tstack-handoff or the card round-trip) and for answering the owner's "what needs me?" in chat (use tstack-owner-desk).

name: tstack-code-tidy
description: Use before you commit or hand over a change: read your own diff and remove what it added that the change doesn't need (debug output, dead code, commented-out code, defensive checks the types already rule out, one-caller wrappers, stray files, names that break the file's own style) without changing behaviour, then prove behaviour held by running the project's tests. Skip for redesigning code (use tstack-architect), for comments that explain code (use tstack-no-comments), and for code the diff didn't touch.

name: tstack-council

name: tstack-create-verification-skill
description: Use when nothing in a project lets an agent start the real app, operate it, and show a change working as a person would see it (a web page, a CLI, an API, a desktop app), or when a reviewer keeps asking for proof you can't produce. Skip when the project already has one (use tstack-maintain-verification-skill), and for unit tests (use tstack-tdd).

name: tstack-decide

If it is, ask once with a question block in a post (one person, two to four options under 80 characters, your pick marked with recommend:, the why under the options), wait with sfora answers, and record the answer on the card as OWNER DECISIONS or PM DECISIONS (date). name: tstack-how
